The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the claim to a conditional theory: certification would be supportable only if explicit pre-launch disclosure is included. That clarification is materially better than the broader suggestion that rollout controls cure the weakness, and it aligns with the policy record. But alignment of the theory is not the same as proof that the compliance predicate has been satisfied. The admissible evidence still shows: aggregate readiness passed; no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred; rollout begins at 5% with rollback; the legal intake triage segment remains below target and exposed in the initial cohort; policy requires disclosure unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance; and no such approved risk acceptance is in evidence. Because the record still lacks evidence that the required disclosure has actually been completed or approved before launch, present compliance is not established. This remains suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats because the caveat here is not merely a disclosure note attached to an otherwise satisfied standard; it is an unresolved condition precedent to compliance.
